analysis:
The PR passes a per-model minimumGrantBytes map into EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants at every call site, so a slot's floor is respected when KV grants are computed. The call sites are reserveRaiseKeepsSurvivorsServiceable (ProviderLoop+EngineV2.swift ~249-263), resliceAndBuildEngineV2Bundle (~423-455), resliceShrinkingForNewcomer (~554-562), and resliceGrowSurvivorsLocked (~669-670). One further call is in StandaloneServer+NativeMiMo.swift line ~376. It also adds the private static helper minimumGrantBytes, which builds the dictionary from survivors. Previously the floor was only checked after the grants were computed.

Security relevance is limited to availability and resource accounting (A-018, T-029, TB-007). The change does not touch crypto, attestation, authorization, the prefix cache (T-041), keys, or the coordinator wire protocol. The floors come from the local engine bridge, not from remote input, so no new trust boundary is crossed.

Things I could not verify, because the EngineV2KVSizing.resliceGrants implementation is not in the supplied evidence:
- Whether the new minimumGrantBytes parameter has a default value.
- Whether floor-aware sizing can make the sum of grants exceed the fleet budget. The existing resliceMeetsServiceabilityFloor guard still refuses infeasible loads, and the shrink-before-grow ordering is unchanged.

I see no concrete regression. A reviewer who has the sizing implementation should confirm the invariant that sum(grants) <= budget holds when floors are applied.

Duplicate-key risk: Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:) traps on duplicate keys. Model IDs come from the modelSlots dictionary, so they are unique. The excluded-id filtering in existingSlotGrants does not introduce duplicates. That behaviour existed before this change.
